procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
AUS 224183 was represented by Richard Longbottom.
CAN 217965 was represented by Allan Clark.
Tim Woodford (CAN 187186) gave evidence as a witness for AUS 224183.
Chris Raab (USA 226424) gave evidence as a witness for CAN 217965.
The hearing is suspended at 18:33 in order to check if there is some evidence from the media, as the day races were broadcasted; the hearing is re-started at 18:47, no video evidence was found.
facts: Wind speed 9 kts, light choppy sea.
The incident occured in the zone of mark 1 at the end of the first beat to windward, race 10.
When entering the zone on port tack, AUS 224183 luffed, passed head to wind and reached a close-hauled course on starboard tack on the starboard layline.
At that time CAN 217965 was on close-hauled port tack on a collision course with AUS 224183, 1 hull lenght to leeward of the port layline.
When about 1.5 m from AUS 224183 and 1 hull lenght from the mark, CAN 217965 suddenly luffed and passed head to wind.

At the same time AUS 224183 luffed, and before CAN 217965 assumed a close-hauled course, a contact with no damage or injury occured between the right aft quarter of CAN 217965 and left side of AUS 224183.
No boat took a penalty turn.
conclusions: After passing head to wind and before reaching a close-hauled course, CAN 217965 failed to keep clear of AUS 224183. CAN 217965 broke RRS 13.
CAN 217965 did not avoid contact with AUS 224183 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for AUS 224183, the right-of-way boat, to avoid contact with CAN 217965 when it became clear that CAN 217965 was not keeping clear. AUS 224183 did not break RRS 14(a).
decision: By not keeping clear of AUS 224183, CAN 217965 broke RRS 13 and is DSQ in race 10.
